title: LoRA: low-rank adaptation
hook: Why two skinny matrices can change a giant one, when they cannot, and what rounding does to a small update.

verified.claim: A LoRA's sum is weight += strength x scale x up @ down, with scale alpha / rank, or 1 with no alpha. The lab's version equals the real one, difference 0.
ModelPatcher merges per module when it fits, and otherwise applies LowVramPatch on each forward pass.
FP8 stores back through stochastic rounding, seeded by the key.
create_train sets up random and down 0.
The tables come from the lab.

unchecked: The low-rank target in the lab is built by hand, and it doesn't test the low-rank hypothesis on diffusion models.
We don't know how large real image LoRAs' updates are against their weights.
Which rounding looks better in a picture is untested.
